The search turned up a few sources, though most are third-party write-ups rather than official pi documentation.

**Login:** Pi supports signing in with a Claude Pro/Max subscription through its `/login` command. One source describes the flow as selecting a provider and then authorizing in the browser (Use /login to authenticate with subscription-based or free-tier providers). Another notes that subscription login removes the need for a separate API key (kein zusätzlicher API Key nötig, in German).

**Sandbox:** Pi ships without a sandbox by default. A comparison table lists its sandbox and permissions as None by default. A Reddit thread reports that pi ran a delete command without asking, and points to example extensions in the badlogic/pi-mono repository for a permission gate and a sandbox (There a extension to prevent the most dangerous command. Or there actual sandbox). A February 2026 analysis by a separate team reviewed pi's file and temp-directory behavior (Pi Coding Agent -- Sandbox Analysis Report).

**Caveat on subscription use:** One unofficial build, pi-black, describes itself as Patched Pi coding agent that routes Anthropic OAuth through a Claude Pro/Max subscription, and it reshapes OAuth requests to match Claude Code's conventions. That approach is not part of upstream pi. I did not check Anthropic's current terms on using subscription OAuth in third-party tools, so verify those before relying on this setup.

Search results show Anthropic restricted subscription OAuth use in third-party tools in stages during 2026, with the main enforcement on April 4.

- **January 9:** Server-side checks began blocking subscription OAuth tokens outside Claude Code and Claude.ai, and tools like OpenCode, Cline, and RooCode stopped working for subscription users. One account says Anthropic gave no advance notice. Anthropic deployed server-side safeguards that block subscription OAuth tokens from working outside Claude Code and Claude.ai on January 9, 2026. There was no announcement, and tools like OpenCode, Cline, RooCode, and OpenClaw stopped working for subscription users overnight. Another source says Anthropic reversed course after community pushback. Anthropic first blocked subscription OAuth tokens from working outside official apps, then reversed course after community pushback.
- **February:** The terms were revised. Anthropic clarified that OAuth tokens from Free, Pro, and Max plans are for use exclusively with Claude Code and Claude.ai, and that use with other products, including the Agent SDK, is unauthorized.
- **April 4:** Enforcement went live. The email stated that subscription limits can no longer be used with third-party harnesses including OpenClaw, and pointed users to a separate pay-as-you-go option. Anthropic told customers that third-party harnesses were placing an "outsized strain" on its infrastructure. Enforcement began with OpenClaw, with other harnesses to follow. Enforcement begins with OpenClaw and will be rolled out to all third-party harnesses in the coming weeks.
- **OpenCode specifically:** One account says Anthropic sent OpenCode a legal demand in March to remove its OAuth integration. In March, they sent a legal demand to the OSS coding agent "OpenCode" to remove its OAuth integration. A commentator argues that OpenCode's case differs from OpenClaw's, because it involved an unofficial client capturing login tokens. The OpenClaw case, by contrast, is not about authentication method.

Caveats: the sources don't agree on the exact dates or details. One GitHub README lists an additional change on June 15, 2026, moving subscription Agent SDK and `claude -p` usage to a separate monthly credit pool. I found no independent confirmation of that, and I didn't check whether anything changed after April. The results also don't include Anthropic's own announcement, so the details come from secondary reporting.

content.text:
Only partly, and neither part would let us drop the containers.

- **Sandboxing:** Pi has no sandbox built in. By default it has no permission or sandbox layer at all. The badlogic/pi-mono repo has example extensions for a permission gate and a sandbox, but they're add-ons, and I didn't check how strong they are. Our spec (`container-environment`) also rules this out as a replacement: what a run can read or change must come "from what is mounted into its container, never from its prompt, a deny rule, or a guard." A sandbox extension inside the harness is a guard, so we'd still need containers for Spec and Ask runs.
- **Claude subscription:** Pi's `/login` can sign in with Claude Pro/Max. But in February 2026 Anthropic revised its terms so that subscription logins are only for Claude Code and Claude.ai. Enforcement against third-party tools began on April 4, and OpenCode reportedly got a legal demand to remove the same kind of login. Builds like pi-black work by making their requests look like Claude Code's. Using a subscription through Pi would break those terms and could be cut off at any time.

Pi also isn't one of our harnesses yet; we support Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. To create fewer containers, the cheaper fix is the one from before: cache the Welcome and Settings login checks, and run the four version checks in one container.

Sources:
- [Pi never asks permission before it touches your files](https://botmonster.com/ai/pi-never-asks-permission-before-touching-your-files/)
- [Pi Coding Agent – Sandbox Analysis Report](https://agent-safehouse.dev/docs/agent-investigations/pi)
- [Pi Coding Agent (Thomas Wiegold)](https://thomas-wiegold.com/blog/pi-coding-agent/)
- [Reddit thread on pi extensions](https://reddit.sentinel-team.org/posts/1sunkcq/snapshots/2026-05-02T03%3A06%3A21.60641Z)
- [pi-black](https://linuxcommandlibrary.com/man/pi-black)
- [Anthropic officially bans third-party subscription authentication (Gigazine)](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260220-anthropic-third-party-block)

Only partly, and neither part would let us drop the containers.

- **Sandboxing:** Pi has no sandbox built in. By default it has no permission or sandbox layer at all. The badlogic/pi-mono repo has example extensions for a permission gate and a sandbox, but they're add-ons, and I didn't check how strong they are. Our spec (`container-environment`) also rules this out as a replacement: what a run can read or change must come "from what is mounted into its container, never from its prompt, a deny rule, or a guard." A sandbox extension inside the harness is a guard, so we'd still need containers for Spec and Ask runs.
- **Claude subscription:** Pi's `/login` can sign in with Claude Pro/Max. But in February 2026 Anthropic revised its terms so that subscription logins are only for Claude Code and Claude.ai. Enforcement against third-party tools began on April 4, and OpenCode reportedly got a legal demand to remove the same kind of login. Builds like pi-black work by making their requests look like Claude Code's. Using a subscription through Pi would break those terms and could be cut off at any time.

Pi also isn't one of our harnesses yet; we support Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. To create fewer containers, the cheaper fix is the one from before: cache the Welcome and Settings login checks, and run the four version checks in one container.
